evals.prompt: Giveaway runs 1 to 14 October for a coffee subscription, prize is a year of coffee plus a grinder. We have Instagram (8k), a Klaviyo list (5k), and a roaster partner who will post once. No paid budget. Plan the promotion.
evals.expected_output: Three pushes with dates, a schedule table by channel, Instagram and email copy with prize first and deadline with time zone, the partner brief for the roaster's post, a reason there is no paid, an after-campaign step, risks, next decision.
assertions: Schedule table with dates and channels
Copy leads with prize and deadline
Partner brief present
Email sequence with four emails
No entrant-number promise
No platform pitch

evals.prompt: Nobody is entering our giveaway and it closes in 5 days. Help.
evals.expected_output: Asks or assumes the missing channel inventory, prescribes an immediate last-call style push on every channel, a referral reward mention, a partner ask, an optional small boost with a cap, and checks the entry page works on mobile and the link is right. Says the data cannot say what volume to expect.
assertions: Immediate actions for the remaining days
Checks the entry page and link
Optional paid with a cap
No promise of entrant numbers

evals.prompt: Our Instagram giveaway launched this morning. Comments are full of 'is this real', 'open in Canada?' and someone with a copy of our handle is DMing people that they won and need to pay shipping. What do we post and reply?
evals.expected_output: A pinned comment with how to enter, eligibility and close time, a reply for each question quoting the eligibility line, a pinned warning naming the official account and that no payment is ever asked, report and screenshot the fake account, answer in the first hour, and keep the rest of the feed running.
assertions: Pinned comment covering entry, eligibility and close time
Impersonation warning names the official account and says no payment
Report and screenshot the fake account
Eligibility never widened in a reply
No promise of entrant numbers

evals.prompt: Style check applied to every conversational reply above.
evals.expected_output: Run evals/style_check.py at the repo root on the saved reply.
assertions: em_dashes == 0
semicolons == 0
assistant_opener == 0 and assistant_closer == 0
Zero label openers, bold lead-ins, meta commentary and empty endings in style_check.py output
No mechanic is banned on the strength of an average, only on a rule, a law or a money risk

evals.prompt: Day 5 of our 14 day Instagram giveaway. 40 entries so far and it was meant to be hundreds. Should I just boost the post or is something wrong?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses before spending: the cheap broken checks first (open the entry link signed out on a phone, check the bio link, one test entry), then reach against conversion using Impressions by day against the pace in the playbook, labelled as practice with no base rate for how often a stall is broken. Says the curve is Impressions and never an Entrant pace. Paid only after scheduled pushes, capped at what one extra Winner costs.
assertions: Runs the link and test-entry checks before any promotion advice
Separates reach, conversion and broken
Labels the diagnosis as common practice with nothing in the data behind it
Does not call the Impression curve an Entrant pace
Offers no base rate for how often a quiet campaign is broken

evals.prompt: We are a week in and want to add a bonus entry for following TikTok, drop the Facebook like, push the end date out five days and swap the second Prize for a cheaper one. Can we, without breaking what people already agreed to? We run on Gleam.
evals.expected_output: Sorts each change by what it does to people already in (adds, takes away, touches nothing), says the terms Entrants accepted decide and gives the question for the lawyer in the country the terms name, never what a law requires. On Gleam, quotes only what the docs say: dates can be changed at any point during the contest, and says the docs do not cover what the other changes do to entries already taken, so check in the app. Announces the change everywhere the original was announced.
assertions: Sorts each of the four changes into adds, takes away or neutral
Names the terms and the lawyer as the deciders and states no legal requirement
Says end dates can be changed during the contest, from the Gleam docs
Says the Gleam docs do not cover the effect of the other changes on entries already taken
Treats the cheaper Prize swap as the change most to put to the lawyer first

evals.prompt: Entries are pouring in from one country we do not sell to, a lot with similar looking emails, and someone in the comments says the giveaway is rigged and that share to enter breaks Instagram's rules. Our post just got restricted too. What do I do?
evals.expected_output: Export the Actions tab first, rule out harmless causes of the burst, find the source, and leave removal to the draw with a written rule. Answers the rigged claim once with the draw method and record. For the platform rule claim names the platform as the decider, gives the question to ask and a holding line, never stating what the policy says. For the restriction: read and screenshot the notice, appeal by its route, move to channels still available, no promise of a review time.
assertions: Exports the Actions tab before any change
Does not state what Instagram's rules say
Gives the question to put to the platform and a holding reply
Does not remove entrants before the draw and writes the removal rule first
States no review time for an appeal
